newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen gets offers for Q1 1997 crude sales - official.
newsitem.headline: Yemen gets offers for Q1 1997 crude sales - official.

text.p: Yemen has received bids from 20 Arab and international companies to buy crude oil for January-March 1997, an oil official said on Monday.
The bids cover 220,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Marib Light and Masila crude, he told Reuters.
"We will study the offers next week...to select the appropriate ones ahead of signing the contracts," he said. He gave no further details.

Tokyo-based traders said last month Yemen had invited bids for crude sales for the first quarter of 1997. It asked for bids to be placed by 1500 GMT on November 25 and be valid until 1500 GMT on December 5.
The official said Yemen offered Marib Light and Masila crude at 25 and 55 cents below Brent respectively -- the same as for the last quarter of this year.
Yemen exports about 100,000 bpd of Masila and 30,000 bpd of Marib Light to Japanese, South Korean and European buyers.
